statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays in the low band because NQ has now surrendered almost the entire overnight advance, trading 29,580.25 (+0.05%) after a roughly 184-point reversal from the 29,764.25 high, while Stress moves to the high band on a fourth day of crude gains, a 4.80% 10-year and a widening split across the index complex.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping resolves to EA_ON for NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD alike. A narrow danger window remains flagged for the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening between 13:30 and 15:00 UTC, where a single auction discounts two sessions of accumulated Gulf, energy and rates news. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ gives back its overnight gain to trade flat at 29,580.25 as Dow futures fall 0.80% and Brent nears $100 ahead of the post-holiday U.S. reopening
body:
U.S. cash equity markets were closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day and reopen at 13:30 UTC today, so the Nasdaq-100 last settled a full cash session on 4 September. NQ futures trade at 29,580.25, up 15.00 points or 0.05% from the 29,565.25 previous close, inside an overnight band of 29,525.00-29,764.25. The decisive change since the previous assessment is the depth of the reversal: NQ tagged 29,764.25 earlier in the session and has since retraced roughly 184 points, giving back essentially the whole advance and returning to the prior settlement. A retracement of that size, without any shallow-pullback sequence, failed-retracement chain or repeated extension, is the opposite of the pathological no-retracement path that threatens mean-reversion methods, and it is the single strongest piece of evidence in this assessment for keeping Tail near its base rate.

Cross-asset confirmation is not merely absent but actively contradictory, and the contradiction has widened again. Dow futures are at 53,012.00, down 428.00 points or 0.80%, in a 52,993.00-53,336.00 band, and S&P 500 futures are at 7,702.00, down 20.00 points or 0.26%, in a 7,698.50-7,728.50 band. A tape in which NQ is flat, ES is down a quarter percent and YM is down four fifths of a percent is a rotation tape, not a directional index trend, and it does not support any trend-up or trend-down label.

The Stress side has strengthened rather than faded. WTI trades at $93.70, up 1.26% on the day, with Brent at $98.38 and within about two dollars of $100, a fourth consecutive session of gains driven by the Strait of Hormuz corridor: the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes over the weekend, Saudi Aramco's Jizan refinery was hit for the second time in a month, and Iran has said an agreement with Oman to manage shipping through the strait is nearing completion. That energy channel feeds directly into an already hawkish rates path. The U.S. 10-year yield is around 4.80%, close to three-year highs, with the 2-year at 4.38%, and futures markets are pricing roughly a 60% probability of a 25 basis point increase at next week's Federal Reserve meeting. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on approximately $20 billion of U.S. goods take effect today, adding a further trade-policy layer. Against that, VIX at 15.30 remains historically low, which is why Stress is placed at the bottom of the high band rather than higher.

The evidence therefore separates cleanly. The environment is difficult and the headline stack is dense, which is a Stress and Confidence matter. The observed price path is two-way, deeply retracing and internally conflicted, which is a Tail matter, and it argues for a low reading. The one genuine structural risk in the next 24 hours is the 13:30 UTC cash reopening, where a single auction must discount three days of accumulated news; that is reflected as a narrow danger window and a conditional forecast peak, not as an assertion that a directional path has been observed.

Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run but its collection timestamp was 2026-09-08T02:19:06Z, more than four hours old and outside the freshness window, so it was treated as stale and used only for discovery. All price, yield, oil and volatility figures above come from independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment and every one of them mapped to EA_ON. Tail sat at 5-7 through the European and early U.S. hours of 7 September, stepped to 9-10 around the 14:00 and 16:00 UTC windows, fell back to 5 into the evening, then held a persistent 7-10 range from 22:00 UTC onward as the overnight NQ advance developed and then reversed. Stress rose from the mid-50s into a stable 62-64 once the weekend Gulf escalation and the crude move were priced, and Confidence recovered from 75 to 84 as live futures evidence displaced the holiday-thinned reads. Dominant mode alternated between normal and mixed and never resolved to a trend label.
outlookSummary: The projection holds Tail inside the low band across all 24 hours, with a shallow rise into the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening and a peak of 14 in the 14:00 UTC hour that still maps to EA_ON. That rise is conditional structural risk from an unusually information-dense reopening auction, not an assertion that a directional path has been observed. Stress runs 63-69, highest across the U.S. cash session, on the unresolved Gulf energy channel and a 4.80% 10-year. Confidence decays from 85 to 61 with distance from the evidence. The stated invalidations are a reclaim of 29,764.25 with no retracement, a European-led break below 29,525.00, or repeated extension after failed retracements once U.S. cash trades; any of those would justify a materially higher Tail than projected here.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: NQ trades 29,580.25, only +0.05% and back near the 29,565.25 prior close after rejecting the 29,764.25 overnight high by about 184 points. That deep retracement, plus ES -0.26% and YM -0.80%, is the opposite of no-retracement structure, so Tail stays low while Stress holds high on oil and rates.
